blocks.text: BATAM, Indonesia — Cooking and bathing became difficult when taps ran dry on Batam, an Indonesian island where residents are protesting as data centers spring up to power the global artificial intelligence boom. The area had suffered a “long drought” caused by low rainfall, the local water utility operator told AFP, as a strong El Niño cycle exacerbates dry weather. But, as in other countries, anger has been directed at the data centers — warehouse-like facilities that keep apps and artificial intelligence tools running, with water often used to cool their humming servers.
